faq.q: Where do these exchange rates come from?
faq.a: From the European Central Bank's euro foreign exchange reference rates. The ECB publishes each currency against the euro; a rate between two other currencies is computed through the euro.
The ECB publishes its reference rates around 16:00 CET on working days. This site keeps one snapshot a day, so the rates are not live quotes; the current one is from {date}.

faq.q: Why are the Taiwan dollar and the Vietnamese đồng missing?
faq.a: The ECB publishes no reference rate for them, and this site does not take rates from other sources or estimate them.

page.title: {fromCode} to {toCode}: {fromName} to {toName} Exchange Rate Today, History and Converter
page.description: 1 {fromCode} = {rate} {toCode} (ECB reference rate, {date}). Conversion table, converter, high, low and average over 30 days, 1 year, 5 years and since {startYear}, and a chart of the history.
page.answer: On {date}, the ECB reference rates put 1 {fromName} ({fromCode}) at {rate} {toCode} ({toName}), and 1 {toCode} at {inverse} {fromCode}.
page.statsNote: Daily ECB reference rates from {from} to {date}; the change compares the first and the last day of each period.
page.chartLabel: Line chart of {fromCode}/{toCode}: {first} on {firstDate}, {last} on {lastDate}, high {high}, low {low}.
page.method: The ECB publishes every currency per euro, so {fromCode}/{toCode} = ({toCode} per EUR) ÷ ({fromCode} per EUR), shown to six significant digits.
page.monthlyNote: Monthly values divide the two currencies' monthly average euro rates.

faqToday.q: What is the {fromCode} to {toCode} rate today?
faqToday.a: On {date}, 1 {fromCode} = {rate} {toCode} and 1 {toCode} = {inverse} {fromCode}, from the ECB euro reference rates. Banks and exchange services quote their own rates.

faqAmount.a: At the ECB reference rate of {date}, {amount} {fromCode} = {value} {toCode}. The conversion tables list more amounts in both directions.

faqRange.a: In the year to {date}, {fromCode}/{toCode} ranged from {y1Low} ({y1LowOn}) to {y1High} ({y1HighOn}), with an average of {y1Avg}. Since {start}, the high was {allHigh} on {allHighOn} and the low {allLow} on {allLowOn}.
